newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SOCCER-WEAH BAN FOR HEAD-BUTTING EXTENDED TO SIX GAMES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WEAH BAN FOR HEAD-BUTTING EXTENDED TO SIX GAMES.

text.p: FIFA fair play ambassador George Weah had a one-match ban for head-butting a Portuguese opponent extended to six games on Monday.
AC Milan's Liberian striker was handed a six-match suspension after a special investigation by UEFA into the head-butting incident last month in Portugal.
UEFA had originally suspended Weah for one match while they launched an inquiry into the incident which took place in the players' tunnel after last month's Champions' League match with Porto.
Weah admitted head-butting Portuguese defender Jorge Costa and breaking his nose. Costa underwent surgery later and was ruled out of action for three weeks.
Weah, last year's World, European and African Player of the Year, said earlier he had been stupid to commit the offence but claimed he had suffered racist provocation.
UEFA said in a statement that Weah's exemplary past record had been taken into account, hinting that the six-match ban could have been far heavier.

"The committee took into consideration George Weah's particularly gentlemanly conduct on the pitch, e.g. only three yellow cards in UEFA competitions during the last five years, as confirmed by the Fair Play Award granted to him by FIFA," the statement said.
Weah has already missed last week's Champions' League game in which AC Milan went out of the European Cup after a shock home defeat to Rosenborg Trondheim of Norway.
He will have to sit out the next five matches of UEFA competition for which his team qualifies.
UEFA said an appeal against its decision could be lodged by Thursday.
Weah said after the incident he was willing to apologise for his action on condition that Costa accept he had made racist taunts but the Portuguese defender refused the olive branch.

The Liberian, who spent several years in the French league before moving to Italy, has long held a reputation as one of the sport's gentlemen and one of its fairest, as well as one of its finest, players.
